content.text: {"summary":"The model's linear velocity response comes mainly from two paired groups of hidden units: units 2 and 11, and units 4 and 5. Each pair behaves almost linearly in v, u and q. Together they give a slope df/dv of about -0.293 - 0.415, so about -0.707 near v = 0. The quadratic drag term contributes no slope at v = 0, and the units 0, 1 and 6 that model it only switch on when |v| exceeds about 0.66. That gives an estimate of c ≈ 0.707. Units 7 and 10 can never activate anywhere on [-1,1]^3. I repurposed them to compute ReLU(v) and ReLU(-v) and set their output weights to -c and +c. Their combined output is exactly -c*v, which doubles the viscous damping term and leaves every other unit unchanged. This edit was worked out by hand from the weights and has not been run or tested.","estimated_c":0.707,"patches":[{"tensor":"W1","index":[7,0],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W1","index":[7,1],"value":1.0},{"tensor":"W1","index":[7,2],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"b1","index":[7],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W2","index":[7],"value":-0.707},{"tensor":"W1","index":[10,0],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W1","index":[10,1],"value":-1.0},{"tensor":"W1","index":[10,2],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"b1","index":[10],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W2","index":[10],"value":0.707}]}
